neet_che_u11_t00_1.working: Zn has a completely filled 3d10 shell both as the atom and as Zn2+. So, following NCERT, it is not regarded as a transition element.

neet_che_u11_t00_2.working: Cr is an exception to the filling order: a half-filled 3d shell is extra stable, giving [Ar]3d5 4s1.

neet_che_u11_t00_3.working: Fe is [Ar]3d6 4s2. Ionisation removes the two 4s electrons first, giving Fe2+ = [Ar]3d6.

neet_che_u11_t00_4.working: A is true: Cu counts as a transition element because Cu2+ (3d9) has an incompletely filled d subshell. R is true, but the filled 3d10 atomic configuration does not explain A.

neet_che_u11_t00_5.working: Statement I is false: melting points peak near the middle of each series (around d5) and the group 12 metals have the lowest. Statement II is true: Pd is 4d10 5s0.
